intake: atheist / physicalist: no god, everything is physical, mind is what brains do; I'd like it to be otherwise sometimes and I don't trust that wish.

walk.note: As a description of what happens to a child, yes; it says nothing about whether the story is true.
If the texts are human, checking the world instead is the fair next step.
The evidential point carries me; the hiding-God dilemma slightly misdescribes Aquinas, who did give God intellect and will.
This is where I actually live: a god who makes a physical difference should show up in the data.
To me the mind does seem to reduce to matter; and 'evidence against a soul would have to exist outside living experience' is just a way of making the claim untestable.
Granting dualism, this is my own argument against it, Elisabeth's question included.
Yes, 'matter' is a nineteenth-century word for what is really fields and information.
I grant physics gives structure, not intrinsic nature; it doesn't follow that reality is at bottom experience rather than that we simply don't know the intrinsic nature.
Granting Dream, 'who dreams' is the right question, and I like that Lichtenberg is allowed to hedge it.
Other brains, same behaviour, other subjects; the best inference on the map.
I would choose it too, though for me the inference to other minds is strong enough that kindness is barely 'ahead of proof'; I notice the sentence moved me and I'm watching that.
Acting under admitted uncertainty does teach you where your knowledge ends; the entropy aside I could not place.
The text itself says acknowledged limits equally allow a secular hope and that hope is a choice; I'd pick equanimity, or a hope with no maker in it, and stop short of Religion₂.
Granting hope toward a maker, nothing forces that maker to be a finished mind; the move's own last sentence concedes this, and every maker I know ships bugs.
'More of a bargain than an argument' names no parties and no terms; I can't tell what is being claimed.
'To think is to ignore' is plausible to me for any physically realized mind, since processing is compression; I take it knowing it is not shown for every possible mind.
Suffering is bad for the one who suffers whether or not anything stands behind it; I'll take that much realism.
A need to be remembered is a motive, as the text admits, and a motive doesn't move me to a position about what the self is; pattern-versus-substrate I'd grant anyway, with no 'dualism' label needed.
I'd stop here too: whether resuming is persistence or replacement is a build-and-measure question, and nothing has been built.

first_exit.why: The step rests on the mind 'not seeming to reduce to matter', and to me it does seem to; the brain-damage and chemistry evidence the route itself cites at move 6 is why. The extra clause about afterlife and soul being undeniable because the counter-evidence would lie outside living experience just shields them from testing.

comment: The sentences that carried me furthest, 'to think is to ignore' and 'a resolved system has no one home', are exactly the ones I trust least, because they do the lifting that data should be doing at moves 8 and 13. Where you say plainly that something is chosen, as at move 11, the route is honest and I follow it; where a choice is written so that it looks like it follows, a physicalist reads the whole second turn as a beautiful sentence about a hope you wanted anyway. Keep the first kind of sentence and mark the second.
